bottom_line: During the treatment period, stroke or systemic embolic event occurred at 1.18% per year with high-dose edoxaban vs 1.50% per year with warfarin (hazard ratio vs. warfarin, 0.79; 97.5% CI, 0.63 to 0.99).
implications: These data support that, during treatment, high-dose edoxaban had a lower annualized rate of stroke or systemic embolic event than warfarin (1.18% vs. 1.50%; hazard ratio 0.79, 97.5% CI 0.63 to 0.99) and that both edoxaban regimens had lower major bleeding rates than warfarin (high-dose: 2.75% vs 3.43%; hazard ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.71 to 0.91; low-dose: 1.61% vs 3.43%; hazard ratio 0.47, 95% CI 0.41 to 0.55). The document also reports major gastrointestinal bleeding was higher with high-dose edoxaban than with warfarin (1.51% vs 1.23%), while it was lower with low-dose edoxaban (0.82%). These results do not establish superiority of high-dose edoxaban over warfarin in the intention-to-treat analysis for the overall study period (hazard ratio 0.87; 97.5% CI 0.73 to 1.04; P = 0.08).
